definition: This page covers the overview’s muscular-endurance outcome, without assuming that strength findings apply identically.
summary: The overview reports improved muscular endurance with resistance training compared with no exercise; its reviewed analyses included standard and home-based training.
whyItMatters: Keep the outcome explicit; the overview does not establish one optimal endurance prescription.
keyTakeaways: The overview reports improved muscular endurance with resistance training compared with no exercise; its reviewed analyses included standard and home-based training.

goalContexts.interpretation: The overview reports improved muscular endurance with resistance training compared with no exercise; its reviewed analyses included standard and home-based training.
qualifiers: Eligible healthy adults aged at least 18 with no defined disease, in resistance-training studies lasting at least six weeks; group results are not individual predictions or clinical/youth guidance.
Most included reviews concerned participants with minimal or no resistance-training experience; some included advanced trainees.
The overview searched reviews through October 2024. Only the identified eligibility and adaptation sections support this extraction.
No independent human, clinical or new GRADE appraisal; overlapping reviews, differing protocols and insufficient variable-specific evidence constrain interpretation.
